title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes combinatorial-topological 'ateliers' via 'magasins' (M, ≤, ≪, |·|) satisfying axioms Mag 1–Mag 4. Here \tilde X = {X' ≤ X}, and 'figures' are subsets of M. The most plausible reading is that ≤ is something like 'is a face/closed piece of' and ≪ is a coarser containment relation, but this is an interpretation. On the previous page he begins a 'polyhedral' variant. M is called prepolyideal if, for every X, \tilde X has the property that two elements bounded above and below have an Inf. For X ≪ Y he then defines X ≪_pol Y to mean: for every Y' ∈ \tilde Y, the induced figure X_{Y'} = \tilde X ∩ Ouv(Y') is empty or has a largest element. In polyhedral language: the trace of X on every face of Y is empty or a single face of X.

On this page:
(0) Prepolyideality is equivalent to X ≤ Y ⇒ X ≪_pol Y, i.e. to reflexivity X ≪_pol X. This is necessary for (M, ≤, ≪_pol, |·|) to be again a magasin. He asks whether it is sufficient and checks the axioms one by one.
(1) Mag 1 reduces to transitivity of ≪_pol. Take X ≪_pol Y ≪_pol Z and a face Z' ≤ Z. Then Y_{Z'} is empty or a single Y'. If empty, X_{Z'} is empty. Otherwise X_{Z'} = X_{Y'}, which is empty or a single X' because X ≪_pol Y. This uses transitivity of induced figures.
(2) Mag 2: for X ≪_pol Y, the set {Z ∈ \tilde Y | X ≪_pol Z} must have a least element (a 'carrier face'). He shows it coincides with {Z ∈ \tilde Y | X ≪ Z}, which has a least element by Mag 2 for M. The key lemma is X ≪ Y' ≤ Y, X ≪_pol Y ⇒ X ≪_pol Y'. This holds because faces of Y' are faces of Y.
(NB) Consequently the 'open' relation for ≪_pol is ≪_pol ∧ \overset{∘}{≪}.

The next page finishes Mag 3 and Mag 4 (trivial, since they involve only ≤ and |·|). It then defines polyideal magasins (≪ = ≪_pol) and the associated polyideal magasin M^pol. This is a reflector-type construction: from a prepolyideal structure one extracts the 'polyhedral' sub-relation of containment for which intersections with faces are faces.
errors: Mag 1 also needs antisymmetry, which is inherited from ≪. Reflexivity holds exactly by the prepolyideal hypothesis (the equivalence stated at the top). Grothendieck does not spell this out, but it is immediate.

Transitivity tacitly uses X_{Z'} = X_{Y_{Z'}} (compatibility of induced figures under composition). He flags this parenthetically ('transitivité des figures induites') but does not prove it on this page.
In Mag 2 the inclusion argument uses that \tilde{Y'} ⊂ \tilde Y for Y' ≤ Y, i.e. transitivity of ≤. This is fine.

ideas.what: Relation X ≪_pol Y: X ≪ Y and the trace of X on every face of Y is empty or a single face of X. This is the 'polyhedral intersection property'.
ideas.modern_name: intersection property of polyhedral / regular CW complexes; face-poset condition 'intersection of two cells is a cell or empty'
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology (Alexander, Whitehead, Zeeman); poset form in Björner's CW posets (1984) and in abstract polytope theory
ideas.where_published: Unpublished 1986 Analysis situs notes (cote 156-8). The broader tame-topology programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984).

ideas.what: Verification that (M, ≤, ≪_pol, |·|) satisfies the magasin axioms when M is prepolyideal (transitivity, existence of a minimal carrier face).
ideas.modern_name: closure of a structure under restriction to a sub-relation; carrier/support face of a subcomplex

ideas.what: Prepolyideal magasins (bounded pairs in each \tilde X have Inf) and the associated polyideal magasin M^pol (on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: meet-semilattice-like face posets; polyhedral complexes as an axiomatic 'atelier'
ideas.usually_credited_to: no direct counterpart; related to Björner's CW posets and lattice-theoretic face-poset characterizations

missed.claim: This is part of an unpublished axiomatic framework ('magasins/ateliers', spatial vs polyhedral) for a combinatorial tame topology. Polyhedral structures are carved out of general ones by the relation ≪_pol and a reflector M ↦ M^pol. The page itself only contains routine verifications; its interest lies in documenting the framework.
missed.quote: ce qui est nécessaire pour que (M, ≤, ≪_pol, |·|) soit encore un magasin. Est-ce suffisant ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of documentary interest for reconstructing Grothendieck's 1986 approach to 'analysis situs' / tame topology. It could be compared with later axiomatic treatments (CW posets, o-minimal cell structures, combinatorial models of stratified spaces).

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine axiom checks (transitivity, minimal carrier face) for a polyhedral variant of an unpublished axiomatic structure. The framework itself is little known, but nothing on this page would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'pri[?] pol[?] idéal' should read 'prépolyidéal' (with 'pré' inserted above).
The displayed implication is X ≤ Y ⟹ X ≪_pol Y (double ≪ with 'pol' under it), not ⋘.
'(M, ≤, ≪_pol, |0|)' should be '|·|'; 'soit encore une magma[?]' should be 'soit encore un magasin. Est-ce suffisant ?'
'(Donc on utilise transitivité des rangs[?] induites[?])' should probably be 'transitivité des figures induites'.
'Y'' ≤ \tilde{Y'}' is better read as 'Y'' ∈ \tilde{Y'} sont aussi ∈ \tilde Y'.
